newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday extended Friday's gains to 16,634.9 points and analysts said more growth was seen on Tuesday and later this week after recent falls and good March earnings data released last week.

"The market should react a little to the falls from 17,500 points at mid-March and there should be a slight growth trend for a few sessions," said Sebastian Buczek, an analyst at ING BSK Asset Management.
Some analysts said this week's 222-million-zloty ($70.9 million) public offering by metals trader Impexmetal SA and 83-million-zloty ($26.5 million) offering by Kredyt Bank could limit the upside.
Other analysts said bourse sentiment might prove strong enough to withstand the heavy primary schedule.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.6 percent on Monday to 16,634.9 points and turnover rose 6.9 percent to 183.8 million zlotys ($58.7 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 68 to 17 with eight stocks flat.

Analysts said most of Monday's top gainers were buoyed by strong March earnings, including electromagnetic transmitter maker Relpol, construction and trading firm Mostostal Export, trader Universal and cable maker BFK, which all rose near or above eight percent.
They said Monday's biggest loser, industrial boilermaker Rafako, fell 9.6 percent after its March loss worsened.
Post-price-fixing buying of Mostostal Export and selling of Rafako were strong enough to reduce investors' bids.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose two percent in 12.4-million-zloty ($4 million) trade and fell 1.6 percent in 15.2-million-zloty ($4.9 million) live trade, where the WIG 20 index rose 0.5 percent.
